the spirolactams are not conformational mimetics of the beta II turns of aplidine and that the peptidyl prolyl cis-trans isomerism at the Pro8-N-Med-Leu7 amide bond is a structural feature of aplidine with a significant influence upon the cytotoxic activity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beta II turn at the side chain does not play a major role in the bioactive conformations of aplidine or tamandarin.

the beta II turn in aplidine and tamadardin A is not a structural element of the bioactive conformations, but the cis/trans isomerization at the Pro8-N-Met-Leu7 amide bond, which is located at the beta II turn, is a crucial element for the bioactivity of aplidine and that the bioactive confromation of aplidine is the cis form at the pyruvic acid-8-amide bond.
the conformationally constrained spirolactam analogues are not cytotoxic, but the cytotoxicity of aplidine and its analogues is not dependent on the presence or absence of the spirolactamic moiety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformationally constrained spirolactam didemnin analogues are inactive, but the conformational constraints do not prevent the binding to the cellular targets.
the spirolactams do not stabilize the beta II turn of the didemnins, which is not essential for their cytotoxicity.

the spirolactams, as well as other conformationally restricted didemnins, are good models for studying the bioactive conformations of these compounds, although they are not suitable candidates for drug development because of their reduced cytotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the fact that the conformation of the beta turn at the side chain is not a determinant for the cytotoxic activity, the conformation of aplidinol (the C-terminal dehydrobutyrine) is a key factor for its activity.
the spirolactams are not a good replacement for the dipeptide Pro-N-Me-d-leucine in aplidine or tamandarin, at least in the case of these analogues, where only the spirolactamic ring is modified.

the conformationally constrained didemnin analogues are not as cytotoxic as aplidine and tamardarin A, which suggests that the conformation of the side chain is not a key determinant for the cytotoxicity of didemnolide analogues.
